f4r.count_explanation: Eight clearly recognizable attached head-like terminals are listed as a partial inventory, not the plant total. Numerous red/green narrow blades also potentially satisfy the terminal rubric, but I cannot reproducibly distinguish all separate stalk-ended bodies from compound overlapping blade groups in this full-source view. I decline to invent a finite total interval. The separate uppermost spray is visibly disconnected or its connecting path is obscured; it is not silently attached to the main graph.
f4r.fork_or_crossing_example: Upper attached three-head spray has a visible convergence of stalks. The colored leaf-like bodies along side branches often meet in tight overlapping groups: treating each color patch as a separate outgoing stalk would change the graph.
ambiguities: Fine pale basal connectors converge above a detached-looking lower root-like object; a single uninterrupted basal connector is not securely traced. Lower structure excluded from the provisional above-stem examples, but this is not a certified full rooted graph.
Uppermost separate spray above the text cannot be joined solely because it is vertically aligned.
Terminal heads alone would ignore qualifying blade-like bodies and would violate the fixed rubric.

f10r.count_explanation: Sixteen candidate terminal bodies are localized; uncertainty in the crowded upper curved-blade stack could merge two candidate units, giving 14–16. This interval is a segmentation uncertainty, not a measured biological count. The upper oval segment on the bent stalk is not counted as a separate terminal because the path continues to the large blue head. Internal blue lobes and leaf teeth are not separately counted.
f10r.fork_or_crossing_example: At the lower broad green pair, two lateral stalks visibly leave the main stem. The crowded curved-blade stack above has overlapping outlines and very close insertion points; exact binary-junction order is not secure.
ambiguities: T04–T07 include crowded outlines; at least two candidate separations are uncertain.
The brown lateral basal structure and its two red bodies are below the distinct erect-stem boundary and excluded under the fixed basal rule.
Local forks are visible, but a complete ordered rooted hierarchy would require observer-specific resolution of crowded insertion points.

f13r.count_explanation: Thirteen small head-like endpoints and six large blade-like bodies are provisionally distinguishable; two narrow inner green bodies may be separate blade terminals or parts of their continuous larger outlines. This gives 19–21 above the basal cut-stem cluster, conditional on that boundary. Top cluster overlaps make individual attachment ancestry uncertain even where head centers are visible.
f13r.fork_or_crossing_example: Broad upper left and right blade paths visibly diverge from the upright stem. At the compact terminal-head cluster, superposed colored tubes do not expose every junction, so a head list cannot determine the tree.
ambiguities: Several erect stalks emerge from distinct circular cut-like ends above the red lower structure. A single shared visible basal hub is not independently clear; joining these through the root-like mass would add an inferred connection.
The lower red mass is morphologically distinct, but the exact root of one above-basal connected graph remains uncertain.
Narrow inner blades may be internal lobes of continuous outlines; teeth and round markings within heads are not terminals.

findings: Several local forks and outlined terminal bodies are recognizable, but I cannot certify two exact complete terminal inventories with reproducible rooted hierarchies. f4r complete enumeration remains unresolved; f10r/f13r have explicit compound-unit/topology ambiguities.
uncertainties: This is a native qualitative observation record, not automated graph extraction.
Counts describe a graphic rubric, not biological leaves, flowers or roots.
The missing complete f4r count is explicitly retained instead of an artificial broad numeric interval.
